implementation_notes: The aggregator collapses into the language: Promise.all(parts) fulfills only after every partial fulfills and yields the merged array in input order, while rejecting as soon as a partial rejects; Promise.allSettled (ES2020) is the wait-for-all-tolerate-failures form because it always fulfills with one status record per input. Correlation and de-duplication remain application concerns: the promises must be created per correlated request, and partials arriving over a channel need a Map keyed by correlation id plus an arrival counter and an explicit setTimeout/AbortSignal.timeout, since no promise combinator has a deadline.
pitfalls: Promise.all rejects on the first rejection and the other results are no longer reachable at the await site - use allSettled or per-promise catch for tolerate-failures aggregation.
Rejections from fire-and-forget partials that nobody awaits terminate recent Node.js processes by default; always attach a handler.
Promise.all returns results in input order and has no timeout: a partial that never settles hangs the await forever unless the combinators are raced with a timer.
